Subject: Nightly ingestion failing with 429s / latency spikes

Kim,

Over the last three nights our nightly batch that ingests patient summaries into our analytics pipeline has been failing intermittently. We're seeing a mix of 429 rate-limit responses and large tail latency (requests taking 6-12s instead of ~200ms). The failures started roughly at 01:00 UTC and lasted for 30-45 minutes each night — that window aligns with the time our largest job runs.

Attached is a small error_log_snippet.txt and a timeline.csv that highlights the 429s and elevated p50/p95 latencies. This is blocking our downstream recon reports and causing several SLA alerts on our side.

Can you please triage urgently and advise whether this is a quota or throttling issue on Redwood's side? We need a mitigation plan and an ETA for a fix. If this is expected behavior after the recent pricing/throughput policy updates, we need to understand options (reserved capacity, temporary credits, configuration changes).

Emily

Kim/Team — I pulled the attached snippet and ran a quick query against the rate-limiter metrics. Preliminary findings:

- The error pattern matches token-bucket exhaustion: a burst of high QPS from Glacial Health around 01:00 UTC consumes the per-minute bucket, then subsequent requests get 429s until the refill period catches up.
- The p95 latency spike is correlated with requests queued at the edge while retry/backoff triggers; some fall back to slower model variants causing the long tail.
- I do see that Glacial Health is on a shared quota class that recently had its burst_window_multiplier lowered in the last policy push (change-req ID: policy-2029-06-18). That adjustment would reduce temporary burst tolerance.

Short-term mitigations I recommend (pick one or more):
1) Apply a temporary account-level override to increase the token_bucket_capacity by 3x for the nightly window (01:00–02:30 UTC) for 48 hours. I can push this as a runtime patch if Karthik approves.
2) Create a per-customer reserved fallback route mapped to a compatible quantized model (lower latency variance) and route batch jobs there during the maintenance window.
3) If override risk is unacceptable, we can introduce client-side advisory headers that recommend smaller batch chunking for the next two jobs.

I’ve prepared a patch (redwood-temp-override.patch) that adjusts the policy store and a short rollback instruction. If we push #1 we should monitor token consumption and SLO impact.

Monica
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-temp-override.patch

> change-req ID: policy-2029-06-18 — lowered burst_window_multiplier for shared quota class

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2029 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Nightly ingestion failing with 429s / latency spikes

Thanks — I dug into the policy store and runtime logs. Root cause summary:

- On 2029-06-18 we shipped a policy tuning that changed the burst_window_multiplier for the "shared_batch_quota" class from 1.5 -> 0.5 to reduce cross-customer interference. That change combined with Glacial Health's high-concurrency batch resulted in the token bucket depleting much faster than before.
- Additionally, a regression in the routing fallback logic meant some jobs were not automatically routed to the compatible quantized model variant (q8_compat) when the primary route hit rate limits. That explains the latency tail.

Planned immediate actions (hotfixes):
- I'll approve and push Monica's runtime override for a 48-hour window for Glacial Health (token_bucket_capacity * 3) to buy time.
- Re-enable the automatic fallback routing to q8_compat for batch endpoints (hotfix PR ready).
- Roll back the burst_window_multiplier change for the "shared_batch_quota" to 1.2 while we run targeted load tests. This rollback will be staged and monitored.

Risk and rollback: the override is reversible; the routing fallback fix is low risk; the policy rollback affects all customers on that quota class so we'll stage it and monitor SLOs across a small cohort.

I'll coordinate the rollout and post back once the override is live.

— Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
